standard.title: First Nations drama and identity
standard.description: investigate the ways that drama created and/or performed by First Nations Australians celebrates and challenges multiple perspectives of Australian identity
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have investigated the diversity of drama created by First Nations Australians, considering culturally responsive approaches and ICIP rights (Y7-8). They understand that First Nations drama is diverse and requires culturally responsive engagement.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate the ways that drama created and/or performed by First Nations Australians celebrates and challenges multiple perspectives of Australian identity.

nodes.label: Australian identity as contested — and drama as a site of that contest
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can articulate that Australian identity is multiple and contested, and identify how drama becomes a site for celebrating and challenging specific versions of that identity.
nodes.minimum_width: Student identifies at least one version of Australian identity that a First Nations drama celebrates and one that it challenges, and names specific dramatic elements doing that work.
nodes.typical_width: Students investigate how and why drama practitioners work collaboratively with communities to develop and present contemporary First Nations Australian theatre; they consider how global trends in drama are influencing First Nations drama; they investigate how contemporary First Nations theatre explores and challenges histories of Australia and Australian identity.
wider: Students compare and critique how contemporary drama from different First Nations communities and non-Indigenous Australian dramatists treat the same historical or contemporary issues — examining whose version of Australian identity is being presented
Students investigate how a specific First Nations drama work has changed in reception over time — what it celebrated or challenged at first performance vs. how it is read now
nodes.hinge_reason: The concept of Australian identity as plural and contested — not a settled shared story — is foundational for the critical analysis this standard demands; without it, students treat First Nations drama as 'different perspective' rather than as a challenge to the dominant frame.

response_modes.reason: Explicitly establish the concept of contested national identity before analysing drama; use comparative examples of how different communities tell the story of Australian identity before analysing how First Nations drama intervenes.

success_criteria: Student articulates that Australian identity is multiple and contested
Student identifies both a celebration and a challenge in a specific First Nations drama work, naming the dramatic elements involved

nodes.label: Investigating how drama celebrates and challenges — global, collaborative, contemporary
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate specific examples of contemporary First Nations drama, analysing how global trends, community collaboration and historical engagement shape celebration and challenge.
nodes.minimum_width: Student investigates at least one contemporary First Nations drama work in depth, analysing how it engages with global trends or community collaboration to celebrate or challenge Australian identity.
nodes.typical_width: Students investigate how global trends influence First Nations drama; they examine how collaborative community development processes produce drama with particular political and cultural dimensions; they compare and critique ways contemporary drama celebrates and challenges influences on Australian identity.
wider: Students investigate how a First Nations drama work navigates the tension between international festival audiences (who may consume cultural difference) and local community audiences (for whom the drama is an act of cultural assertion)

Students investigate the relationship between First Nations drama and legal or political history — land rights, sovereignty, recognition — and how specific dramatic works have been shaped by or have shaped those histories

response_modes.reason: The diversity of contemporary First Nations drama — in form, purpose, community context and global reach — is extensive; engagement with multiple works prevents students from treating any single work as representative.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Contemporary First Nations Australian theatre is diverse, politically engaged, globally connected and rapidly developing; students who investigate widely gain much richer appreciation of its scope and significance within and beyond Australian cultural life.
success_criteria: Student analyses at least one contemporary First Nations drama work in depth — addressing global trends, community context, or historical engagement
Student explains both what the work celebrates and what it challenges in relation to Australian identity
Student engages with cultural authority and appropriateness in their investigation
